name: Immutable
description:
An immutable object, exhibiting immutability, is an object that can't be changed. It may be created, read and cloned. On the other hand, a mutable object may change when one of its method is called, even if this is not visible from the outside.

Immutable objects are thread-safe. 

Immutable objects often return a clone version of themselves, after modification.
code:
<?php

    class Elephpant {
        private $age = 0;

        function inc() : self {
            $return = clone $this;
            $return->age +=1;

            return $return;
        }
    }

    $elephpant = new elephpant();
    $olderElephpant = $elephpant->inc();

    // $elephpant and $olderElephpant are two distinct objects

?>
